title: Deuteronomy Chapter 20 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Deuteronomy chapter 20 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 20 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Deuteronomy Chapter 20.

questions.question: In Deuteronomy 20, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The priest shall approach and speak to the people
Officers shall speak to the people about those who built a new house
God tells not to be afraid when seeing horses and chariots
The command about men betrothed to a wife returning home
questions.correctAnswer: God tells not to be afraid when seeing horses and chariots
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:1 is the first verse and it contains the instruction not to be afraid when seeing horses and chariots.

questions.question: Who is said to go with the Israelites to fight against their enemies?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:4 states that the LORD your God is the one who goes with you to fight for you against your enemies.

questions.question: What is the role of the priest when the Israelites come near to battle?
options: To approach and speak unto the people
To lead the army into battle
To build new houses for the people
questions.correctAnswer: To approach and speak unto the people
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:2 states that the priest shall approach and speak unto the people when they come near to battle.

questions.question: What does the priest tell the people about their hearts when facing battle?
options: Let not your hearts faint, fear not, and do not tremble
questions.correctAnswer: Let not your hearts faint, fear not, and do not tremble
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:3 instructs the people not to let their hearts faint or be afraid or terrified.

questions.question: What reason is given for why the Israelites should not be afraid of their enemies?
options: For the LORD thy God is with thee, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt
Because their enemies are few in number
Because they have no horses or chariots
questions.correctAnswer: For the LORD thy God is with thee, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:1 states that the LORD thy God is with you and brought you out of Egypt, which is the reason not to fear.

questions.question: What should a man do if he has built a new house and not dedicated it when the officers speak to the people?
options: Let him go and return to his house
Let him fight in the battle
questions.correctAnswer: Let him go and return to his house
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:5 says that a man who has built a new house and not dedicated it should return to his house lest he die in the battle.

questions.question: Why should a man who has planted a vineyard and not yet eaten of it return home?
options: Lest he die in the battle and another man eat of it
Because he is not a good soldier
Because the vineyard must be guarded
Because he is not allowed to fight
questions.correctAnswer: Lest he die in the battle and another man eat of it
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:6 explains that a man who has planted a vineyard and not eaten of it should return home lest he die and another eat of it.

questions.question: What instruction is given about a man who has betrothed a wife but not taken her?
options: Let him go and return to his house
Let him fight in the battle
Let him marry her before the battle
questions.correctAnswer: Let him go and return to his house
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:7 instructs that a man betrothed but not yet married should return home lest he die and another man take her.

questions.question: What does the priest say about trembling or being terrified before battle?
options: Do not tremble, neither be ye terrified
questions.correctAnswer: Do not tremble, neither be ye terrified
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:3 commands the people not to tremble or be terrified before battle.

questions.question: What phrase does the LORD use to describe His action in relation to the Israelites in battle?
options: To fight for you against your enemies, to save you
To leave you to fight alone
questions.correctAnswer: To fight for you against your enemies, to save you
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:4 clearly states that the LORD fights for you against your enemies to save you.

questions.question: Who speaks to the people about those who have built new houses or planted vineyards or betrothed wives?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:5-7 shows that the officers speak to the people regarding those with new houses, vineyards, or betrothed wives.

questions.question: True or False: The priest encourages the people to be afraid when they see many enemies with horses and chariots.
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:1-3 instructs the people not to fear or be afraid when seeing enemies with horses and chariots.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD your God is said to go with you to fight for you against your enemies.
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:4 states that the LORD your God goes with you to fight for you against your enemies.

questions.question: True or False: The officers allow a man to stay and fight if he has recently built a new house but has not dedicated it.
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:5 says such a man must go and return home lest he die in battle and another man dedicate the house.

questions.question: True or False: The text says that men who have vineyards can send someone else to fight for them instead of returning home.
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:6 specifies that the man who has planted a vineyard and not eaten of it must return to his house, not send someone else.

medium.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 20 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Deuteronomy Chapter 20 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What should a fearful and fainthearted man do according to Deuteronomy 20:8?
questions.explanation: According to Deuteronomy 20:8, a fearful and fainthearted man should return to his house to prevent his brethren's hearts from fainting as well.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 20:9 promise will happen if the officers make captains after speaking to the people?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:9 states that after the officers finish speaking, they shall make captains of the armies to lead the people, thus organizing the army.

questions.question: What should be proclaimed when approaching a city to fight according to Deuteronomy 20:10?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:10 instructs that when approaching a city to fight, peace should be proclaimed to it.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 20:11 say will happen if a city responds with peace?
questions.explanation: According to Deuteronomy 20:11, if the city answers peacefully, all the people will become tributaries and serve.

questions.question: What is the directive in Deuteronomy 20:12 if a city will not make peace?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:12 instructs that if a city will not make peace, then it must be besieged.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 20:13, what should be done to every male after the city is delivered into the hands of the Israelites?
options: They should be smitten with the sword
questions.correctAnswer: They should be smitten with the sword
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:13 states that every male should be smitten with the edge of the sword when the city is delivered.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 20:14 permit the Israelites to do with the spoil of their enemies?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:14 allows the Israelites to take the spoil of their enemies and eat it as given by the LORD.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 20:1, what should the Israelites remember when facing a battle?
options: The LORD your God is with you
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD your God is with you
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:1 reassures the Israelites that they need not be afraid because the LORD their God is with them.

questions.question: What consequence is highlighted in Deuteronomy 20:5 for a man who has built a new house but has not dedicated it?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:5 states that if a man has built a new house and has not dedicated it, he should return home lest he die in battle.

questions.question: What must a man do if he has planted a vineyard but has not yet eaten of it according to Deuteronomy 20:6?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:6 says that a man who has planted a vineyard and has not eaten should return to his house to avoid dying in battle.

questions.question: What should a man who has betrothed a wife do according to Deuteronomy 20:7?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:7 instructs a man who has betrothed a wife and has not taken her to return to his house to avoid dying in battle.

questions.question: If a man is encouraged by the priest before battle, what should he do according to Deuteronomy 20:3?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:3 encourages the people to let not their hearts faint and fear not when facing battle.

questions.question: Is it true that Deuteronomy 20:4 says the LORD fights for the Israelites against their enemies?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:4 affirms that the LORD your God goes with you to fight for you against your enemies.

questions.question: Is it false that Deuteronomy 20:12 commands to make peace with a city that will not make peace?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:12 actually commands to besiege a city that will not make peace, not to make peace with it.

questions.question: Is it false that the spoils taken from enemies are to be shared equally among all Israelites according to Deuteronomy 20:14?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:14 states that the Israelites shall take the spoil for themselves, not share it equally.

hard.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 20 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Deuteronomy Chapter 20.

questions.question: What shall be done to the cities that are very far off from the Israelites?
questions.explanation: This is stated in Deuteronomy 20:15, which specifies that for cities very far off, a different approach is taken compared to those in the immediate land of the inheritance.

questions.question: What were the Israelites commanded to do to the cities of the nations given to them?
questions.explanation: This directive is found in Deuteronomy 20:16, emphasizing the complete destruction of those cities.

questions.question: Which groups were specifically mentioned to be utterly destroyed?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:17 lists the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, and others as nations to be destroyed as commanded by God.

questions.question: What was the reason for the total destruction of these cities?
options: To prevent sin against the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: To prevent sin against the LORD
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:18 explains that the destruction is to prevent the Israelites from being influenced by the abominations of those nations.

questions.question: What should not be destroyed when besieging a city?
questions.explanation: According to Deuteronomy 20:19, trees that bear fruit should not be destroyed because they provide sustenance.

questions.question: What type of trees should be destroyed during a siege?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:20 clarifies that only trees that are not for eating can be cut down.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'שָׁלָל' (shalal) in Deuteronomy 20:14 mean?
questions.explanation: In Deuteronomy 20:14, the term 'שָׁלָל' refers to the spoils taken from the defeated enemies.

questions.question: What literary technique is used in Deuteronomy 20:17 regarding the nations?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:17 uses inclusio by starting and ending with a list of nations, framing the command to destroy them.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of divine warfare found in Deuteronomy 20:4?
questions.explanation: Romans 8:31 echoes the assurance of God's support in battles, paralleling Deuteronomy 20:4's message of divine assistance.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage fulfills the command to destroy the Canaanite nations mentioned in Deuteronomy 20:17?
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:21 describes the Israelites executing the command to destroy all in Jericho, fulfilling the command from Deuteronomy 20:17.

questions.question: What comes before Deuteronomy 20:15?
options: A command to destroy all enemies
A description of cities to besiege
questions.correctAnswer: A command to destroy all enemies
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:14 precedes 20:15 with instructions about taking spoils and dealing with enemies, setting the stage for the directives in 20:15.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 20:19 emphasize about the trees during a siege?
options: They can be used for weapons
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:19 highlights that trees are vital for life, thus should not be destroyed unnecessarily during a siege.

questions.question: The command to utterly destroy the nations is an example of what?
questions.explanation: The command in Deuteronomy 20:17 reflects divine judgment against the nations for their abominations, emphasizing God's holiness.

questions.question: The Israelites were to fear their enemies according to Deuteronomy 20:1. True or False?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:1 instructs the people not to be afraid of their enemies because God is with them, therefore the statement is false.

questions.question: The trees that bear fruit should be destroyed according to Deuteronomy 20:19. True or False?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:19 explicitly states that trees for food should not be destroyed during a siege, making the statement false.

theological.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 20 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Deuteronomy Chapter 20 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Deuteronomy 20:1 teach about God's nature in relation to His people in battle?
options: God is sovereign and actively fights for His people
God is indifferent to human warfare
God promises automatic victory regardless of obedience
God requires human strength alone for victory
questions.correctAnswer: God is sovereign and actively fights for His people
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:1 emphasizes that the LORD is with His people and fights for them, showing His sovereignty and active involvement in their salvation in battle.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning human weakness and divine provision is taught in Deuteronomy 20:8?
options: God acknowledges human fear and allows the fearful to withdraw
God demands perfect courage from every soldier
Fearful soldiers must be forced to fight regardless
Human fear is a sin to be punished
questions.correctAnswer: God acknowledges human fear and allows the fearful to withdraw
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:8 teaches that those who are fearful and fainthearted are allowed to return home, showing God's accommodation of human weakness to preserve communal morale.

questions.question: What doctrine about holiness and separation from pagan influence is taught in Deuteronomy 20:17?
options: God commands the utter destruction of certain nations to prevent idolatry
God tolerates pagan practices among His people
God requires assimilation of all conquered peoples
God's holiness permits the coexistence with pagan nations
questions.correctAnswer: God commands the utter destruction of certain nations to prevent idolatry
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:17 commands the complete destruction of certain Canaanite nations to prevent Israel from adopting their abominations, emphasizing God's call to holiness and separation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Deuteronomy 20:4 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:4 shows God's faithfulness in going with His people to fight and save them, fulfilling His covenant promises.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated in Deuteronomy 20:19 regarding treatment of trees in siege warfare?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:19 demonstrates God's providence by instructing preservation of fruit trees during siege, reflecting care for human life and future provision.

questions.question: How does the chapter's teaching on besieging cities (Deuteronomy 20:10-17) connect with the theme of divine judgment in later Scripture?
options: It prefigures God's ultimate judgment on sinful nations
It contradicts New Testament teachings on love
It promotes human autonomy over divine will
It minimizes the seriousness of sin
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures God's ultimate judgment on sinful nations
questions.explanation: The divine command to destroy certain nations echoes God's final judgment themes seen throughout Scripture, including Revelation's depiction of judgment on wicked nations.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 20:1-4 prepare believers for reliance on God as their warrior in the New Testament?
options: It anticipates Christ as the divine warrior who fights for salvation
It teaches reliance on human military strength
It denies the need for faith in spiritual battles
It emphasizes political alliances over divine help
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates Christ as the divine warrior who fights for salvation
questions.explanation: The LORD fighting for Israel prefigures Christ's ultimate victory over sin and death, teaching believers to rely on divine power rather than human might.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 20:16 and 20:17 teach about God's justice and holiness?
options: God’s justice requires complete destruction of idolatrous nations to maintain holiness
God permits partial tolerance of pagan nations
God’s holiness allows coexistence with Canaanite peoples
God’s justice is limited to punishment of individuals only
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice requires complete destruction of idolatrous nations to maintain holiness
questions.explanation: Verses 20:16 and 20:17 together command utter destruction of specific nations to prevent idolatrous influence, highlighting God's justice intertwined with holiness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 20:5 and 20:6 teach about sanctification and the value of temporal blessings?
options: Temporal blessings require dedication and are grounds for exemption from battle
Temporal blessings are irrelevant to spiritual duties
God forbids enjoying vineyards and houses before battle
questions.correctAnswer: Temporal blessings require dedication and are grounds for exemption from battle
questions.explanation: Verses 20:5 and 20:6 show that those who have new houses or vineyards not yet dedicated are exempted from battle, teaching respect for sacred dedication and valuing God's blessings.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 20:10 and 20:12 teach about God's justice and mercy in warfare?
options: Peace is offered first, but war is just if peace is refused
God demands war without offering peace
Peace must be forced regardless of enemy response
Mercy is never extended to enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Peace is offered first, but war is just if peace is refused
questions.explanation: Verses 20:10 and 20:12 teach that peace must be proclaimed first; only if refused is war justified, showing God’s balance of justice and mercy.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Deuteronomy 20:13-17 promotes unjust genocide. What does this passage actually teach?
options: It commands holy war to prevent idolatry and preserve covenant purity
It indiscriminately commands killing of all peoples
It encourages conquest for economic gain only
It suggests assimilation of pagan practices
questions.correctAnswer: It commands holy war to prevent idolatry and preserve covenant purity
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:13-17 commands destruction of specific nations to guard Israel from idolatry and covenant unfaithfulness, reflecting God’s righteous judgment, not indiscriminate genocide.

questions.question: What doctrine about leadership and community responsibility is taught in Deuteronomy 20:9?
options: God ordains structured leadership for orderly conduct in battle
Each soldier acts independently without accountability
Officers are chosen based on wealth
questions.correctAnswer: God ordains structured leadership for orderly conduct in battle
questions.explanation: Verse 20:9 shows God’s provision of captains to lead the people, teaching the doctrine of divinely appointed leadership and communal order.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated in Deuteronomy 20:18?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:18 emphasizes that God commands destruction of nations to prevent Israel from imitating abominations, revealing His holy nature demanding purity.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Deuteronomy 20:7 and 20:8 teach about sanctification and the role of the community in spiritual warfare?
options: Personal readiness affects communal strength and victory
Individual status has no impact on community
Personal fears are irrelevant to spiritual battles
questions.correctAnswer: Personal readiness affects communal strength and victory
questions.explanation: Verses 20:7 and 20:8 demonstrate that personal circumstances and fear affect not only the individual but the entire community’s morale and sanctification in battle.

questions.question: How does the command in Deuteronomy 20:19 regarding not destroying fruit trees during siege reflect God’s providential care in redemptive history?
options: It acknowledges the preservation of life and future provision amid judgment
It shows indifference to human welfare
It promotes environmental destruction during war
It commands total annihilation without exception
questions.correctAnswer: It acknowledges the preservation of life and future provision amid judgment
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:19 teaches that trees producing food must be spared to provide for life even during warfare, reflecting God’s providence sustaining His people.
